mechanism_narrative: Persistently depressed WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate weak commuter flows, and that same demand weakness keeps retail visits below the prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain at or below their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while GROCERY_PHARM remains deeply negative, households are substituting away from discretionary shopping trips and RETAIL_REC falls within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 20 points and GROCERY_PHARM below -40 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 20 points while GROCERY_PHARM stays below -40 points.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly drop in TRANSIT signals worsening access to commercial districts, and retail-and-recreation mobility slips on the following week even if other categories are flat.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall in the next 7 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop of at least 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain far below baseline, the constraint is not supply-side commuting but demand suppression, so RETAIL_REC keeps drifting down over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -65 points and TRANSIT below -65 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both staying below -65 points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility can pull discretionary out-of-home time toward outdoor leisure, which diverts trips from shopping districts and leaves RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains above its current level or continues rising.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to deteriorate while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, households consolidate trips and avoid discretionary retail, producing a lower RETAIL_REC average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM below -50 points while RESIDENTIAL stays above 25 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM drops below -50 points with RESIDENTIAL above 25 points.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES begins recovering from its current trough while TRANSIT remains depressed, commuting can restart before leisure shopping does, causing RETAIL_REC to rise with a lag over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points week-on-week while TRANSIT remains below -65 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points while TRANSIT stays below -65 points.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of persistently weak TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a broad mobility slump, and unless either series rebounds, retail-and-recreation mobility will stay below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean over the next 28 days without a rebound in either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.
